questions.question: One-third of a journey is covered at a speed of 25 km/h, the next one-third of the journey is covered at a speed of 40 km/h and the remaining journey is covered at a speed of 50 km/h. The average speed (in km/h, rounded off to 1 decimal place) for the entire journey is:

n = 3

If a distance is divided in 'n' equal parts each travelled with different speeds, then

Average Speed = (n)/(frac{1){S₁}+(1)/(S₂)+(1)/(S₃)+....+(1)/(S_n)}

Where, n = Number of equal parts

**Calculation:**

Average Speed = (3)/(frac{1){25}+(1)/(40)+(1)/(50)}

⇒ Average Speed = (3)/(frac{8){200}+(5)/(200)+(4)/(200)}

⇒ Average Speed = 3 ÷ (17/200)

⇒ Average Speed = (3 × 200)/17 = 35.29 ≈ 35.3 km/h

**∴ The average speed for the entire journey is 35.3 km/h.**

questions.question: Father’s age is three times the sum of ages of his two children, After 6 years, his age will be twice the sum of the ages of both the children. The age of the father is:

x = 3 (a+b)\:\x=3a+3b ... equation 1

After 6 years,

 x +6= 2(a+6+b+6)\:\x+6=2(a+b+12)\x+6=2a+2b+24\:

Now let us equate equation 1 and equation 2:

3a+3b=2a+2b+18\a+b=18

questions.question: What is an aquifer?

options.text: Pockets of freshwater trapped in sandy beds in a desert
Sheets of frozen water found in rocky caves at high altitudes
Water that flows through natural channels in an estuary
Water stored underground between layers of hard rock

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water stored underground between layers of hard rock**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **An aquifer** is the rock layer that **contains water and releases it in appreciable amounts. **
 
• This rock contains **water-filled pore spaces**, It is observed that when the spaces are connected, the water can flow through the matrix of the rock. An aquifer is also called a water-bearing stratum.
 
• Rocks like granite and schist are poor aquifers as they have very low porosity. 
 
• When rocks are highly fractured, they make good aquifers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• At the time when **a water-bearing rock readily transmits water to wells and springs then** it is called an aquifer. Wells can drill into the aquifers and water can be pumped out.
 
• Precipitation help to add water (recharge) into the porous rock of the aquifer.
